stack.name: Glow Blend
stack.positioning: A three-peptide vial sold by research-peptide vendors as a simpler, KPV-free variant of the Klow blend, combining a copper peptide with two tissue-repair peptides; marketed for recovery, wound healing, and skin/collagen support.
stack.rationale: GHK-Cu is included primarily for its collagen-synthesis and wound-healing signaling. BPC-157 and TB-500 are frequently combined with each other on their own (see the tb-500-bpc-157 research pairing) for proposed complementary tissue-repair mechanisms. There are no controlled trials evaluating this three-peptide combination as a whole — the rationale here is inferred from each peptide's individual, largely preclinical mechanism, not from data on the blend itself.
stack.ratio_source_note: Multiple independent research-peptide vendors list a 70mg vial containing 50mg GHK-Cu, 10mg BPC-157, and 10mg TB-500 (a 5:1:1 ratio by mass). This figure was consistent across every vendor listing checked; some vendors also offer smaller vial sizes (e.g. 30mg) at the same ratio. No manufacturer-published label or independent third-party lab panel breakdown of actual vial content was available to verify it independently.
caution_notes: Combined effects of these three peptides used together have not been studied — safety data exists only for each peptide individually, and mostly from preclinical/animal models.
BPC-157 and TB-500 are on the WADA Prohibited List at all times (S2); GHK-Cu is not FDA-approved for injectable use.
None of these three peptides has an FDA-approved human indication.
stack.disclaimer: For research and educational purposes only. This is not medical advice. This blend is not FDA-approved. Consult a licensed healthcare provider before using any peptide.

components.role: Copper peptide included for collagen-synthesis, wound-healing signaling, and skin/dermal support; the majority component by mass in this blend.
Proposed gastroprotective and angiogenic peptide via nitric-oxide pathway signaling; one of the most frequently stacked research peptides.
Proposed to promote cell migration and angiogenesis via actin sequestration (thymosin beta-4 fragment).
